name: Pulmonary Capillary Hemangiomatosis

criteria.description: Histopathological evidence of proliferation of pulmonary capillaries within alveolar septa
Presence of pulmonary arterial hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as pulmonary veno-occlusive disease and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Characteristic radiologic findings on high-resolution CT including diffuse ground-glass opacities and septal thickening

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of capillary proliferation plus evidence of pulmonary hypertension and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires lung biopsy; clinical and imaging findings support diagnosis but are not definitive alone.

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating right heart strain
Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: High-resolution CT showing diffuse ground-glass opacities and septal thickening
Pulmonary arterial hypertension on right heart catheterization
genetic: No well-established genetic mutations identified; rare familial cases reported
other: Histopathology demonstrating capillary proliferation within alveolar septa
Exclusion of pulmonary veno-occlusive disease by pathology

distinguishingFeatures: Histopathology shows venous and venular occlusion rather than capillary proliferation
Different radiologic pattern with more septal thickening and lymphadenopathy
Absence of capillary proliferation on histology
Different clinical course and response to therapy

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure with hemodynamic compromise
references: Montani D, et al. Pulmonary Capillary Hemangiomatosis: A Review. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2013.
Eyries M, et al. Pulmonary Capillary Hemangiomatosis and Pulmonary Veno-Occlusive Disease: Clinical and Pathological Features. Eur Respir J. 2016.
Simonneau G, et al. Updated Clinical Classification of Pulmonary Hypertension. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2013.
